prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key pledges and policies (max 500 words)

Economy, tax and pensions
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: uprate State Pension and introduce an age-related personal allowance so the State Pension remains below the tax threshold.
- Maintain National Living Wage at two-thirds of median earnings (c. £13/hour on current forecasts).
- Raise at least £6bn/year by tackling tax avoidance/evasion.

Business, innovation and infrastructure
- Maintain corporation tax; keep/extend full expensing (seek to include leasing when affordable).
- 10‑point plan for SMEs (business rates support, prompt payment, finance access, reduced reporting).
- Public R&D to £22bn/year; large compute clusters; advanced manufacturing plan; maintain R&D tax reliefs.
- Gigabit nationwide by 2030; standalone 5G in all populated areas.
- Reallocate £36bn from HS2 phase 2 to regional roads, rail and buses; speed up planning approvals to one year for major projects.
- Support aviation (SAF mandate) and maritime; automated vehicles on roads next Parliament.

Work, welfare and families
- Reform disability benefits (PIP) and Work Capability Assessments from Sept 2025; overhaul fit notes to specialist work/health professionals.
- Tougher conditionality: review at 12 months for long‑term unemployed; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill for DWP.
- Childcare: 30 hours free from 9 months to school by Sept 2025; Family Hubs in every local authority.
- Child Benefit to be assessed on household income, tapering from £120k to £160k.

Education and youth
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19; two hours’ PE weekly; statutory mobile‑phone bans in schools; parental access to teaching materials.
- 100,000 additional apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑outcome degree courses.
- Expand SEN places; register for children not in school.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 12‑month paid military/cyber placements (competitive) or 25 days civic service.

Health and social care
- NHS spending to rise above inflation annually; recruit +92,000 nurses and +28,000 doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgeries; 50 Community Diagnostic Centres; 40 new hospitals by 2030.
- £3.4bn tech modernisation: NHS App as single front door; AI diagnostics; Federated Data Platform; cut 5,500 management posts.
- Dental Recovery Plan; NHS service commitment for new dentists.
- Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; expanded mental health support (school teams to 100%, early support hubs).

Borders, security and defence
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn for munitions; minimum 5% of defence budget for R&D (+2% exploitation); National Defence and Resilience Plan; enhanced veterans’ rights.
- Legal annual cap on migration (work/family visas), falling each year; higher salary thresholds; health checks/IHS changes.
- Implement Illegal Migration Act; monthly Rwanda flights; six‑month asylum processing; more returns deals.

Crime and justice
- +8,000 neighbourhood police; hotspot policing nationwide; Martyn’s Law.
- Tougher sentences (including domestic murders); ban SIM farms; cold‑call ban on financial products.
- Four new prisons; more removals of foreign national offenders.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Annual North Sea oil/gas licensing; new gas plants for security.
- Treble offshore wind; deliver CCUS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; retain fracking moratorium.
- Lower policy costs/levies vs 2023; review standing charges; energy‑efficiency vouchers and £6bn for insulation; protect best farmland from solar; onshore wind with local consent.
- Maintain record flood defence funding; Plan for Water (tougher penalties, river restoration); new National Park; tree/peat programmes; stronger waste crime penalties; deposit return scheme; restrict new incinerators not yet built.

Housing and communities
- Build 1.6m homes; fast‑track brownfield; lift London densities; development corporations; mitigate nutrient neutrality via fees.
- Permanent first‑time buyer SDLT threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy; leasehold reform (cap ground rents, end forfeiture misuse); Renters Reform with court changes then abolish Section 21; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Backing Drivers Bill: no road pricing; local referendums for LTNs/20mph; reverse London ULEZ expansion; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways.

Equality, law and society
- Clarify “sex” in Equality Act as biological sex; single legal sex; implement Cass Review; single‑sex accommodation rights in NHS.

Farming and fisheries
- Increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn over Parliament (inflation‑proofed); legal food security target; fast‑track farm infrastructure; five‑year tapered seasonal worker scheme; replicate £100m Seafood Fund.

Union and regional
- Continue direct UK investment (Shared Prosperity Fund extension, Community Ownership Fund, Towns endowments); protect internal market; Intertrade UK; specific transport/energy commitments for Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland; implement Windsor Framework.
